newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW may need more jobs to meet Passat demand.
newsitem.headline: VW may need more jobs to meet Passat demand.

text.p: Strong demand for the new version of the Passat saloon may prompt German carmaker Volkswagen AG to consider adding about 400 jobs to its plant in Emden, Germany, a Volkswagen official said on Friday.
VW spokesman Hans-Peter Blechinger said the carmaker's works council had called on VW to add a minimum of 400 positions but he said no decision had yet been made.

He said the works council may opt to not approve any additional overtime at the plant in order to create new jobs despite plans for VW to boost annual Passat production to about 400,000 units to meet the strong demand.
But Blechinger said excess workers in Wolfsburg may be sent to Emden to help produce the sought-after updated saloon, a possibility rejected by the works council.
"There is currently no area in a VW factory where there are excess workers, also not in Wolfsburg," VW works council leader Hans-Juergen Uhl said.

German union IG Metall said the issue of creating new jobs at VW was a reason for calling off a third round of wage talks on Thursday amid the union's demand for VW to create up to 1,000 jobs and contribute to lowering German unemployment.
VW responded by saying it would review opportunities to hire new workers.
